identity.title: Cardamonin attenuates SH-SY5Y neuronal apoptosis induced by LPS-activated microglia via modulation of the EGFR/PI3K/AKT1/ERK/NF-kappaB pathway.

content.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Microglial activation-induced neuroinflammation plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases. Cardamonin (CD, 2',4'-dihydroxy-6'-methoxychalcone), a natural chalcone flavonoid present in several medicinal plants, demonstrates significant anti-inflammatory activity. Nevertheless, the precise mechanisms by which it mitigates neuroinflammation remain incompletely understood. METHODS: In this study, the potential targets and pathways of CD were investigated using network pharmacology and molecular docking. The neuroinflammatory protective mechanisms were examined in vitro using LPS-stimulated BV2 cells and a BV2/SH-SY5Y co-culture system, employing ELISA, RT-qPCR, Western blot, immunofluorescence, and other assays. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: Network pharmacology identified epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), rac-alpha serine/threonine-protein kinase (AKT1), heat shock protein 90 alpha family class B member 1 (HSP90AB1), prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2 (PTGS2/COX-2) and transcription factor p65 (RELA) as key potential targets, with the EGFR/PI3K/AKT1, MAPK/ERK, and NF-kappaB signaling pathways being the main enriched pathways. In BV2 cells, CD suppressed LPS-induced production of IL-6, IL-1beta, TNF-alpha, and nitric oxide (NO), and modulated the EGFR/PI3K/AKT1/ERK/NF-kappaB signaling axis. Pharmacological inhibition of EGFR or PI3K phenocopied the effects of CD, supporting the functional involvement of this pathway. Additionally, CD attenuated reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and prevented the loss of mitochondrial membrane potential. In a co-culture model, CD pretreatment reduced BV2-conditioned medium neurotoxicity toward SH-SY5Y neurons. Collectively, these findings suggest that CD alleviates neuroinflammation through modulation of the EGFR/PI3K/AKT1/ERK/NF-kappaB pathway, mitigating inflammatory and oxidative stress responses and providing indirect neuroprotection, supporting its potential application in neuroinflammation-associated neurodegenerative diseases.
